note: Inputs of the release after dashboard-data-20261006, read by scripts/finish_haiku55.py. The release folds Claude Haiku 5.5 onto release dashboard-data-20261006 and installs Max's rulings of 2026-10-06: d1022 (the reference adversary's eight confirmed or ambiguous cells) and d994 (the two Louisiana cells). Ten outputs leave scoring for every model; the references, the incumbents' predictions and every earlier exclusion's value stay as they were.

rulings.d1022: exclude the reference-adversary's confirmed cells: engine defects in scenario_018 (AZ) and scenario_025 (OH) state income tax and scenario_043 (CO) and scenario_082 (NY) state refundable credits, and the dependent-return scope cells in scenario_123 (PA) and scenario_093 (MO) federal and state income tax; regenerate the four defect cells in a later release once fixed policyengine-us versions land (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9928, #9925, #9946, #9948); scenario_026 refuted (Max 2026-10-06, 'approve')
rulings.d994: exclude scenario_051 and scenario_077 Louisiana state income tax; keep the published-amounts convention (no change to Idaho 076, SNAP 008/038/109, Maryland 068); version 2 states indexed amounts in the prompt (Max 2026-10-06, 'approve')
rulings.d1029: open (household scope for version 2); the d1022 exclusions of scenario_123 and scenario_093 stand until it is decided

derivation_insert.text: On 2026-10-06 ten more outputs were excluded on review of release dashboard-data-20261006 (reference_audit/2026-10-05-reference-adversary and reference_audit/2026-10-05-louisiana); their records are computed on policyengine-us 2.15.17, whose values are the references.

restated_adjudications.prior: regenerated on 2026-09-22 (capital gain distributions; PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#8839), and scored until this release

adjudications.reasoning: The frozen reference is 1,146.05; the corrected value is 1,137.30. Arizona's 2026 single standard deduction is $16,100: HB 4168 set $15,750 subject to A.R.S. 43-1041(H), which indexes it as the federal basic standard deduction is indexed (Rev. Proc. 2025-32). policyengine-us 2.15.17 carries $15,750 into 2026 unindexed, because the uprating sits on a parent parameter node that policyengine-core does not propagate to the filing-status children. Found by the reference adversary on 2026-10-05 and verified independently (reference_audit/2026-10-05-reference-adversary/verification/independent/az_018.md).

The frozen reference is 1,921.57; the corrected value is 1,916.60. Ohio deducts unreimbursed medical care above 7.5% of federal AGI, with medical care defined by IRC 213(d), which includes insurance premiums (R.C. 5747.01(A)(10)(b)-(c)). policyengine-us 2.15.17 counts premiums only for a person who is Medicare-eligible and has no employer-paid plan, where the form's worksheet line 3 reads 'Medicare or an employer-paid health care plan', so this filer's $6,500 of after-tax premiums get no credit. Found by the reference adversary on 2026-10-05 and verified independently (verification/independent/oh_025.md).

The frozen reference is 19.00; the corrected value is 0.00. C.R.S. 39-22-2003(2) allows Colorado's sales tax refund for a tax year only if the fiscal year ending in it had excess state revenues; every forecast published before the freeze put FY 2025-26 below the Referendum C cap, with a tax year 2026 refund of $0 in every tier. policyengine-us 2.15.17 pays the six-tier refund without that condition. Found by the reference adversary on 2026-10-05 and verified independently (verification/independent/co_043.md).

The frozen reference is 820.35; the value under the published figure is 820.26. The reference rests on a 2026 Louisiana standard deduction of $12,835, which policyengine-us computed from published CPI-U under R.S. 47:294(B) but which no Louisiana publication stated before the 2026-07-03 freeze; Louisiana's first 2026 return amount, $12,838, came in Revenue Information Bulletin 26-019 on 2026-09-28. Excluded under decision d994, which keeps the published-amounts convention for every other reference (reference_audit/2026-10-05-louisiana).

The frozen reference is 667.00; the corrected value is 1,187.61. For tax years from 2026, N.Y. Tax Law 606(c-2) (L.2026, ch. 59, Part A) gives a refundable credit of the applicable percentage of qualifying care expenses, and 606(c)(1) limits the old formula to earlier years. policyengine-us 2.15.17 still computes the 2026 credit as a percentage of the federal credit. Found by the reference adversary on 2026-10-05 and verified independently (verification/independent/ny_082.md).

The frozen reference is 8,628.99; the alternative is 11,848.99. A dependent with $45,000 of wages must file their own federal and state return, and the engine computes only the head and spouse's return. The output definitions name no return, tax unit or household, the prompt shows one tax unit and asks for quantities 'for this household', and careful readers split both ways (reference_audit/2026-10-05-reference-adversary/verification/independent/pa_123.md, verification/definition_conformance.md). Excluded under decision d1022 until decision d1029 settles the scope for version 2.
